subject: Materials Science
title: Why Metals Corrode
description: Learn Why Metals Corrode in one minute.

hook.text: Iron ore is iron oxide. We smelt it into pure iron. Then nature rusts it back to iron oxide.

buildup.text: Corrosion is an electrochemical process — metals lose electrons and return to their natural oxide state.

discovery.text: It requires an anode (metal dissolving), a cathode (electrons consumed), an electrolyte, and a circuit.

twist.text: Gold and platinum resist corrosion because they're thermodynamically stable — they don't want to be oxides.

climax.text: Corrosion costs the global economy over $2.5 trillion per year — about 3.4% of world GDP.

punchline.text: Nature wants its metals back — corrosion is just chemistry being patient.

quiz.question: What drives metallic corrosion?
options: Electrochemical reactions where metals lose electrons
